collection: TOEFL iBT 2026 original spoken-response selection practice
note: Original classroom practice in the current response-selection task family. The official Updated Test Overview illustrates four written response choices. Keep examiner scripts and answers hidden. No recorded audio or adaptive delivery is supplied.
examinerInstructions: For each item, read its examinerScript aloud at a natural pace while the learner sees the prompt and response options. The learner selects the most appropriate reply. Award one classroom practice point for the correct choice. These points have no TOEFL scale conversion.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Listen to the request about a notebook and choose the most appropriate reply.
options: Not at all. Let me put it in my bag.
Yes, I wrote those notes yesterday.
The notebook has a blue cover.
I usually sit near the window.
questions.answer: Not at all. Let me put it in my bag.
questions.explanation: The speaker politely asks for space. The reply agrees and removes the notebook.
questions.examinerScript: Would you mind moving your notebook so I can sit here?

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Choose the reply that responds directly to the study-group invitation.
options: The library closes late on Fridays.
Thanks. I’ll come once my lab ends.
I borrowed that book last week.
Lunch is cheaper in the main cafeteria.
questions.answer: Thanks. I’ll come once my lab ends.
questions.explanation: The reply accepts the invitation and explains when the listener can join.
questions.examinerScript: A few of us are revising in the library after lunch. Would you like to join us?

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Select the response that recognises the speaker’s suggestion about a presentation.
options: I printed the slides on both sides.
The projector belongs to the department.
Good idea. I’ll open with a short case.
The presentation is in the morning.
questions.answer: Good idea. I’ll open with a short case.
questions.explanation: The speaker suggests adding an opening example. The reply accepts that suggestion.
questions.examinerScript: Your slides are clear, but an example at the start might help people see why the topic matters.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Choose the most appropriate response to the offer about carrying a model.
options: The model took three days to build.
The door was painted last term.
I carry my books in a backpack.
Yes, please. I need both hands for this.
questions.answer: Yes, please. I need both hands for this.
questions.explanation: The speaker offers practical help. The reply accepts and explains why it helps.
questions.examinerScript: That model looks awkward to carry. Shall I hold the door for you?

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Select the reply that answers a question about which draft to submit.
options: Yes, that’s the version I need.
I sent my application last month.
The course has three assignments.
A conclusion comes at the end.
questions.answer: Yes, that’s the version I need.
questions.explanation: The listener asks which version is intended. The reply confirms the relevant draft.
questions.examinerScript: When you said to send the revised draft, did you mean the one with the new conclusion?

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Choose the reply that acknowledges the speaker’s apology about an appointment.
options: The rooms are numbered along the corridor.
These appointments last twenty minutes.
That happens. Are you free tomorrow afternoon?
I have already bought a new diary.
questions.answer: That happens. Are you free tomorrow afternoon?
questions.explanation: The reply acknowledges the mistake and proposes a new appointment.
questions.examinerScript: I’m sorry I missed our appointment. I wrote down the wrong room number. Could we arrange another time?

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Choose the response that fits the speaker’s proposal for completing shared work.
options: Wednesday follows Tuesday.
That works. I’ll send you the link.
The report is about urban transport.
The meeting room has a large screen.
questions.answer: That works. I’ll send you the link.
questions.explanation: The speaker offers online review as an alternative to meeting. The reply accepts it.
questions.examinerScript: I can’t meet on Wednesday, but I could review our report online that evening.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Pick the reply that addresses the student’s concern about asking a question.
options: The seminar starts at eleven.
The classroom has forty seats.
I bought the textbook online.
Go ahead. Others may be wondering the same thing.
questions.answer: Go ahead. Others may be wondering the same thing.
questions.explanation: The reply reassures the student that asking can benefit other listeners too.
questions.examinerScript: I’m worried this question is too basic to ask during the seminar.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Choose the response that engages with the concern about a survey conclusion.
options: You’re right. We should consider both explanations.
The timetable is on the noticeboard.
I prefer surveys with short questions.
We printed the charts in colour.
questions.answer: You’re right. We should consider both explanations.
questions.explanation: The speaker questions a causal interpretation. The reply accepts the need to consider another explanation.
questions.examinerScript: I see why you linked the change to the new timetable, but we haven’t ruled out the weather.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Choose the reply that shows understanding of the advice about starting a task.
options: I left my sports bag in the gym.
The application has several pages.
Okay, I’ll begin with the personal details.
The office opens at nine tomorrow.
questions.answer: Okay, I’ll begin with the personal details.
questions.explanation: Get the ball rolling means make a start. Beginning one section follows that advice.
questions.examinerScript: You don’t have to finish the whole application tonight. Just get the ball rolling.

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Select the response that confirms the arrangement for collecting equipment.
options: The recording is about fifteen minutes long.
Exactly. The technician will be at the service desk.
We used a different recorder last year.
I prefer taking notes by hand.
questions.answer: Exactly. The technician will be at the service desk.
questions.explanation: The reply confirms the proposed collection and return arrangement and supplies a useful detail.
questions.examinerScript: So I collect the recorder from you, then return it to the technician after class, right?

questions.subject: Listening
questions.learningObjective: Identify speaker intent and select a pragmatically appropriate reply in a single exchange.
questions.prompt: Choose the reply that responds appropriately to the condition on borrowing a book.
options: The tutorial is on the second floor.
I prefer the previous edition.
There are six chapters in the book.
Thanks. I’ll return it on Thursday.
questions.answer: Thanks. I’ll return it on Thursday.
questions.explanation: Returning the book on Thursday satisfies the stated condition.
questions.examinerScript: You can borrow my copy as long as I get it back before Friday’s tutorial.
